He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. ==Early life== Gray grew up playing [[American football|football]] and started playing basketball at age nine.{{cite web |last=Walsh |first=Chuck |date=April 21, 2020 |title=Growth spurt helps Gray's basketball quest |url=https://capitaloutlook.com/site/growth-spurt-helps-grays-basketball-quest |access-date=September 15, 2023 |website=Capital Outlook}} He attended [[Dillard High School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]. Gray played the [[point guard]] position despite being {{convert|6|ft|8|in}} and {{convert|260|lb}}. As a junior, he led Dillard to the Class 6A state title.{{cite web |last=Lyon |first=Fabian |title=Dillard's dynamic duo is back to defend title |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/article116589563.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |date=November 22, 2016}} In his senior season, Gray won the Class 7A state title.{{cite web |last=Brown |first=A. Richard |title=Class 7A Final: Dillard rolls over Edgewater |url=https://www.theledger.com/sports/20170304/class-7a-final-dillard-rolls-over-edgewater |website=[[The Ledger]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |date=March 4, 2017}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] over offers from [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].{{cite web |last=Lammer |first=Pat |title=Dillard star RaiQuan Gray pledges Florida State |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/fl-recruiting-commitment-announcements-0809-20160808-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |date=August 8, 2016}} ==College career== Gray [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first year at Florida State. As a freshman, he averaged 3.9 points in 12.3 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Weiler |first=Curt |title=New-look RaiQuan Gray reaping rewards of offseason work for FSU basketball |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2021/01/26/florida-state-fsu-mens-basketball-raiquan-gray-body-transformation-seminoles-nba-leonard-hamilton/6695232002/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |date=January 26, 2021}} Gray averaged six points and 3.8 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Anthony |title=Florida State Basketball: Raiquan Gray a key piece for Seminoles in 2020-21 |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/09/22/florida-state-basketball-raiquan-gray-key-piece-seminoles-2020-21/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=March 3, 2021 |date=September 22, 2020}} He improved his conditioning in the offseason. On February 13, 2021, he recorded a career-high 24 points and 12 rebounds in a 92–85 win over [[2020–21 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]].{{cite web |last=Ferrante |first=Bob |title=RaiQuan Gray lifts No. 17 FSU to win over Wake Forest in OT |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-state-seminoles/os-sp-fsu-basketball-0214-20210213-iurehuq32naypm2jpkljlghhoi-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |date=February 13, 2021}} As a junior, Gray averaged 11.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game, earning Third Team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] honors. On April 2, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Schoffel |first=Ira |title=Seminoles star forward RaiQuan Gray declares for NBA Draft |url=https://floridastate.rivals.com/news/seminoles-star-forward-raiquan-gray-declares-for-nba-draft |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=April 2, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn / Long Island Nets (2021–2023)=== Gray was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 59th pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Nee|title=RaiQuan Gray selected by the Brooklyn Nets with the No. 59 pick in the 2021 NBA Draft|url=https://247sports.com/college/florida-state/Article/RaiQuan-Gray-Florida-State-Seminoles-Basketball-2021-NBA-Draft-Brooklyn-Nets-168471215/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=July 29, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} Gray was later included in the roster of the Nets for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Demetris|last=Sapp|title=Brooklyn Nets announce summer League roster|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/08/03/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} On October 25, 2021, Gray was included in the training camp roster of the [[Long Island Nets]], Brooklyn's [[NBA G League]] affiliate.{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets announce training camp roster|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-announce-training-camp-roster-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=October 25, 2021}} On September 26, 2022, Gray signed with the Brooklyn Nets, but was waived on October 15.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-complete-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2022|access-date=October 16, 2022}}{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Chris Chiozza and Raiquan Gray|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-chris-chiozza-and-raiquan-gray|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=October 16, 2022}} On November 4, Gray was named to the opening-night roster for the Long Island Nets.{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Complete 2022-23 Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-complete-2022-23-roster/n-5895915|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} On April 8, 2023, Gray signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Raiquan Gray to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-raiquan-gray-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 8, 2023|date=April 8, 2023}} On April 9 he made his NBA debut in the Nets' final regular-season game, scoring 16 points, with 9 rebounds and 7 assists. However, he was waived on July 18.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive RaiQuan Gray|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-raiquan-gray|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 18, 2023|date=July 18, 2023}} ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2023–2024)=== On September 27, 2023, Gray signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],{{cite tweet|first=Keith|last=Smith|title=The San Antonio Spurs have signed RaiQuan Gray to a training camp deal, a league source told @spotrac.|number=1707158841958273478|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=September 27, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} but was waived two days later.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Spurs Waive Millner, Gray Ahead Of Camp|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/spurs-waive-millner-gray-ahead-of-camp.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|access-date=October 1, 2023|date=October 1, 2023}} On October 31, he joined the [[Austin Spurs]]{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2023-24 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster/n-6027310|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2023|access-date=November 14, 2023}} and on March 2, 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with San Antonio.{{cite tweet|first=Tom|last=Orsborn|title=#Spurs make the following moves reported earlier official: 1, They've converted Barlow's two-way deal to a standard NBA contract; 2, They've signed RaiQuan Gray and Jamaree Bouyea to two-way deals; 3, They've waived forward Mamadi Diakite.|number=1764032846534959265|user=tom_orsborn|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}} On July 8, 2024, Gray was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in a three-team trade also including the [[Sacramento Kings]]{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Harrison Barnes|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-acquire-harrison-barnes|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2024|access-date=July 13, 2024}} and on July 13, he was waived by the Bulls.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Bulls Waive RaiQuan Gray|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/bulls-waive-raiquan-gray.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 13, 2024|access-date=July 13, 2024}} ===AEK Athens (2024–2026)=== On September 22, 2024, Gray signed with [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite web|title=Στη «Βασίλισσα» ο ΡαϊΚουάν Γκρέι|url=https://www.aekbc.gr/sti-vasilissa-o-raikouan-gkrei/|website=AEKBC.gr|date=September 22, 2024|access-date=September 22, 2024|language=Greek}} On August 1, 2025, Gray renewed his contract with AEK for one more season.{{Cite web |last=Papadopoulos |first=Christos |date=2025-08-01 |title=Contract extension with Gray |url=https://www.aekbc.gr/en/contract-extension-with-gray/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=AEK BC |language=en-US}} On March 26, 2026, he was named the MVP of the Round of 16 of the [[Basketball Champions League|BCL]].{{Cite web |title="A mismatch nightmare" - RaiQuan Gray is MVP of the Round of 16 |url=https://www.championsleague.basketball/en/news/a-mismatch-nightmare-raiquan-gray-is-mvp-of-the-round-of-16 |access-date=2026-03-26
